item.title: Compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller with single-measurement direct control
item.description: arXiv:2607.20987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polarization controllers (PCs) and their control algorithms are critical for compensating environmental disturbances and maintaining signal fidelity in polarization-sensitive photonic systems. However, existing controllers often involve trade-offs among key performance metrics,while associated control algorithms either converge inefficiently or require multiple state-of-polarization (SOP) measurements. This work presents a compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller (LC-PC) with balanced overall performance, featuring low insertion loss (<1 dB), low driving voltage (<6 V), and full Poincar\'e sphere coverage. The device exhibits highly predictable and repeatable polarization modulation characterized by SOP-independent trajectory normal vectors, enabling a single-measurement direct-calculation algorithm using pre-characterized rotation axes and voltage-to-rotation relationships, with degree-level polarization control accuracy. The combination of this compact deterministic LC-PC and its efficient control scheme provides a practical solution for polarization management in quantum key distribution, optical sensing, and advanced photonic systems.
item.dc:creator: Ren-De Liu, Jie Wang, Dong-Dong Li, Xian-Chang Du, Dao-Zhong Xiao, Shuai Li, Chuan-Yang Ding, Yan-Lin Tang, Yang Li, Sheng-Kai Liao, Teng-Yun Chen, Shi-Biao Tang

item.title: Evolutionary stability and payoff equivalence in an Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein quantum game
item.description: arXiv:2607.21103v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS) is a strategy that, once adopted by a population, cannot be invaded by any sufficiently rare alternative (mutant) strategy. We analyse evolutionary stability in an Eisert--Wilkens--Lewenstein (EWL) quantization of a symmetric $2\times2$ coordination game, whose classical mixed equilibrium $p^*=1/2$ is not an ESS. In the restricted two-parameter EWL strategy space, the corresponding quantum strategy is a strict symmetric Nash equilibrium and an ESS for every entanglement strength $\gamma>0$. In the full $SU(2)$ strategy space it remains a Nash equilibrium, but in the unreduced game, in which every unitary is a distinct strategy, exact payoff duplicates preclude strictness and ESS for every pure strategy. For the agreement-payoff class, the payoff factors through a Bloch map; identifying payoff-equivalent unitaries gives the reduced space $U(1)\backslash SU(2)\cong S^2$, where strictness and ESS are restored for $\gamma>0$. An arbitrarily small perturbation outside this class that preserves $p^*=1/2$ yields a profitable deviation, so the reduced-space result is not generic.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Iqbal, Derek Abbott

item.title: Bimodal non-Gaussian photonic states from a single quantum emitter in a waveguide
item.description: arXiv:2608.03658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the generation of deterministic and heralded non-Gaussian states of light, using a single two-level system coupled to a chiral waveguide. We study the case of a single two level system driven by pulsed coherent and squeezed drive in a chiral waveguide. For coherent input pulses, we show that the emitter can deterministically generate Wigner-negative states, albeit of limited rank. Going beyond, using squeezed-vacuum inputs, we show that the interaction produces rich bimodal non-Gaussian states from which higher-stellar-rank states, including large squeezed cat states, can be experimentally extracted with a substantial success rate. For experimental feasibility and comparison, we analyze the effect of imperfect coupling and of the intrinsic $50\%$ collection limit of symmetric, non-chiral waveguides. Following that, we propose a simple interferometric scheme that recovers an effectively chiral interaction in an otherwise bidirectional waveguide.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Copie, Ofer Firstenberg, G. P. Teja, Radim Filip, Hanna Le Jeannic

item.title: Photon localization: a comparative study
item.description: arXiv:2608.04134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compare different measures for photon localization in terms of two-dimensional Gaussian wave packets of width Delta k. We find that all measures start to coalesce if the wave packet has evolved for times which are larger than a few (c Delta k)^{-1}. However, the Landau-Peierls wave function yields the largest initial offset <r>-ct > 0 while the Fourier transform of the helicity components of the k-space wave packet yields the smallest offset <r>-ct > 0 and converges towards <r>-ct = 0 fastest. We also discuss local detection of photons through a model detector consisting of ions in ion traps. The position-dependent detection probabilities are inferred from the scattering matrix. We find that the local detection probability for photons can be expressed in terms of three of the proposed localization measures, viz. the Landau-Peierls wave function, the energy wave function, and the Hawton density. Those three proposals also remain close throughout the time evolution of the single-photon wave packet. However, the energy wave function is locally related to electromagnetic fields and is therefore confirmed as the preferred tool for the description of local photon densities. The novelty of our observations concerns three items, viz. the possibility to express local photon absorption matrix elements through three of the proposed localization measures, the coalescence of all the proposed localization measures after sufficiently long evolution of a photon wave packet, and the striking differences of some of the proposed localization measures during early wave packet evolution.
item.dc:creator: Laura M. Ferguson, Ricardo Rojas Castellano, Kayla Oltman, Joshua G. Fenwick, Rainer Dick

item.title: State-resolved quantum-information fingerprints of partial dynamical symmetry in the interacting boson model
item.description: arXiv:2608.04486v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial dynamical symmetry (PDS) is an algebraic structure in which a symmetry is neither exact nor fully broken: a subset of eigenstates keeps good quantum numbers and stays solvable while the rest mix. It is currently identified from spectroscopy. We ask whether it also leaves a purely structural mark in the eigenstates, and find, for the $sd$-IBM Hamiltonians studied here, that it does, though not in the magnitude of entanglement. The diagnostic is the variance of a symmetry Casimir, the label variance $\Var\,\C[G]$, which shares its zero with a block-coherence entropy and a block impurity: all three vanish when a state occupies a single Casimir sector, a single irreducible representation once conjugate representations are resolved by the cubic Casimir. Resolved state by state, the variance is numerically zero on the symmetry-selected subset and large on the mixed states, isolating the PDS states from the wavefunctions alone; the separation does not close as the boson number grows and persists at Leviatan's first- and second-order critical points, whereas the magnitude of bipartite $s|d$ entanglement does not separate the two families. We anchor the analysis in $^{168}$Er, reproducing Leviatan's fitted $\su3$ admixtures and his Hamiltonian-parameter-independent $\gamma\!\to\! g$ $B(E2)$ ratios. The diagnostic also has an exact dynamical form, a Casimir Loschmidt echo rigid on the symmetry-pure states, and we demonstrate its readout on an IBM superconducting processor at $N=3$, where a single solvable/mixed exemplar reproduces the predicted pattern within finite-shot uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Dhritimalya Roy

item.title: Compound beams for direct experimental comparison of quantum operations
item.description: arXiv:2608.09518v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compound beams composed of simple experimental blocks (detected in simultaneous detection windows) that form specific quantum-correlated structures are suggested for simulating the properties of different quantum operations used for creating highly nonclassical and entangled multi-mode states needed in quantum communication, metrology, and information protocols. Qualitative and quantitative comparison of multi-photon addition and subtraction in compound multi-mode thermal as well as sub-Poissonian beams and multi-mode twin beams with their intensities extending over two orders in magnitude is provided. Adding and subtracting up to twenty photocounts, optimal conditions for the generation of experimental nonclassical states are identified. In general, photon addition is identified as advantageous over photon subtraction for the multi-mode thermal and sub-Poissonian beams: It induces (enhances) the nonclassicality in the former (latter) state. Contrary to this, photon subtraction outperforms photon addition in the multi-mode twin beams. Moreover, exploiting temporal photon-pair correlations in compound twin beams when post-selecting, nearly ideal experimental photon(s) addition is demonstrated. The results apply for the beams with mean photon number per mode much less than one.
item.dc:creator: Kishore Thapliyal, Jan Perina Jr., Pavel Pavlicek, Antonin Cernoch

item.title: Q-Edge: Symmetry-Reduced Quantum Simulation of Structured Extreme Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2609.03706v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-dimensional simulation of multivariate extremes is fundamentally limited by the combinatorial complexity of dependence, often more than by the scarcity of extreme observations. We show that symmetry admits a lossless orbit-space representation that preserves structured extreme dependence while replacing an exponentially large dependence space with a compact set of symmetry classes. Based on this principle, we develop Q-Edge (Quantum Extreme Dependence Engine), a symmetry-reduced quantum framework that operates directly in orbit space, enabling scalable simulation and digital twins of structured extreme systems. By transferring symmetry into the data representation rather than the quantum circuit, Q-Edge allows unconstrained quantum generative models to exploit dramatically reduced state spaces. For a 30-dimensional problem, approximately 1.6 million angular states collapse to 256 orbit states, reducing the required quantum representation from about 21 qubits to 8. Our results establish a general computational principle for scalable quantum simulation of structured extreme dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Zhang, Paolo Recchia, Jianlong Lu, Ying Chen

item.title: Time-Dependent Quantum Monte Carlo for fermions: from Bayesian conditioning to spinor dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2609.08415v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo method represents a many-electron state by an ensemble of replicas, in which each electron is described by a cloud of walkers which samples its density in physical space, one walker and one guide wave per replica, and it replaces the Hartree potential by a conditional interaction built from the walker positions. The sampling is in physical space rather than in configuration space, which keeps the cost polynomial. Here we derive that conditional interaction. Treating the walker as a localization of its electron to a finite resolution, we show that Bayes' theorem and a single empirical substitution yield the Nadaraya-Watson form which the method has used heuristically. The nonlocality length then becomes the width of the conditioning, and the pair and mean-field limits follow from one construction. Because the conditioning removes the gauge freedom which eliminates the orthonormality multipliers in Hartree-Fock, we enforce orthonormality by a term derived from the constraint. We generalize the formulation to spinors, where the Pauli suppression at coincidence becomes graded by the local spin alignment, and it reduces through the collinear and mean-field limits to the known two-particle spin equations. For two electrons in a double quantum dot in an inhomogeneous magnetic field, compared with the exact solution, the spinor equations reproduce the non-collinear spin geometry which collinear calculations cannot represent and recover the larger part of the entanglement missing from a single determinant. In the crossover between the exchange and the Zeeman regimes, where the singlet-triplet coherence sets the spin geometry, the replicas must carry that coherence themselves, as in the spin-coupled pair of valence-bond theory.
item.dc:creator: Ivan P. Christov

item.title: The cost of direction in quantum Bell certification
item.description: arXiv:2609.10162v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Certifying a quantum bound can require more information than realizing the correlations that attain it. We show that this distinction becomes unbounded when a proof must condition on one party's measurement question. A fixed Bell scenario attained by one entangled qubit pair has a standard degree-two sum-of-squares certificate, yet the minimum degree in either conditioning direction grows as the inverse square root of the distance to a local endpoint. Choosing the better party does not remove this cost. The obstruction also survives approximate certification: bounding the quantum maximum to any fixed fractional accuracy relative to its Bell advantage requires the same diverging level. Thus a short standard proof cannot be transferred to a uniformly bounded conditioned level, even after relaxing exactness and optimising the direction. Mixing directions within a proof removes this family's obstruction, while a separate finite separation establishes its limits. Contact geometry explains the cost and connects it to a sharp precision law for randomness certification.
item.dc:creator: Fumin Wang

item.title: Quantum models of interaction Hamiltonians and their paradoxes
item.description: arXiv:2609.11618v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In quantum physics it is commonplace to model the interaction of remote systems with a many-body Hamiltonian. Taking such an action-at-a-distance description {\it \`a la lettre} leads to various paradoxes related to faster-than-light communication and apparent inconsistencies in local energy accounting. It also neglects residual effects, such as entanglement between the remote systems and the mediator that implements the interaction, or the decoherence that arises when the remote systems undergo local evolution. We study simple microscopic quantum models that respect the light cone by design and reproduce two-body Hamiltonians. For these models we quantitatively analyze the residual effects of the microscopic mediator on the remote systems, including dressing of stationary states, and decoherence in the presence of fast local control. We show how the models resolve the paradoxes.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Gisin, Serge Massar, Jef Pauwels, Pavel Sekatski

item.title: Exact quantum circuits for a Heisenberg triangle with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
item.description: arXiv:2609.15411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct short analytical quantum circuits for the exact evolution of a spin triangle with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction. We consider pure DM interaction with arbitrary real couplings and two Hamiltonian families with uniform Heisenberg exchange. For pure DM, a change of basis reduces the evolution to two single-qubit rotations. The circuits reproduce the full evolution operator at arbitrary time with a fixed gate count and admit implementations with both triangular and linear qubit connectivity. Experiments on a superconducting IBM quantum processor demonstrate directional quantum-state transfer and reproduce the amplitude and phase of transverse magnetization. In these experiments, the exact circuits reduce distortions relative to circuits based on the second-order Trotter formula. On a 12-spin kagome cluster, exact triangle blocks reduce the gate count at a prescribed accuracy. We also investigate the reduction of coherent errors by adjusting circuit angles and applying echo pulses to neighboring qubits.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Zhukov

item.title: Regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergences
item.description: arXiv:2609.17517v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Barycentric R\'enyi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum R\'enyi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric R\'enyi divergence (called the minimal one) was known to admit an explicit expression. Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric R\'enyi divergence on invertible inputs. This in turn implies that if at least two of the $D^{q_x}$ are strictly larger than the Umegaki relative entropy (in a precise sense), then the resulting barycentric R\'enyi divergence is not even weakly additive.
item.dc:creator: Mil\'an Mosonyi

item.title: Classical Cellular Automaton for Measurement-Only Entanglement Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2609.28743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a generalized classical long-range stochastic cellular automaton that exactly captures the entanglement dynamics and transitions of a measurement-only monitored quantum system. The corresponding quantum model consists of a one-dimensional qubit chain subject to competing single-site and long-range Bell measurements, with separations drawn from a power-law distribution. At every step of each trajectory, the state remains a tensor product of Bell pairs and unpaired qubits, with bipartite entanglement entropy fully encoded in a classical matching of the sites. This exact representation allows us to solve the dynamics analytically in several limits and to determine the steady-state scaling of the entanglement entropy. We find volume-law, fractal, and area-law regimes. Numerical results show that these regimes persist beyond the analytically solvable limit. Because Bell measurement outcomes change only the Bell-state labels and leave the matching unchanged, all subsystem entropies are outcome independent, avoiding the exponential cost of trajectory postselection often encountered in experimental studies of measurement-induced entanglement dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Will Holdhusen, Bailey M. McAmis, Armin Rahmani

item.title: SQD-Agent: LLM-driven agentic framework for Quantum Chemistry workflows
item.description: arXiv:2609.39302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum algorithms and quantum hardware are advancing towards a promising paradigm for scientific applications. However, translating domain-specific problems into executable hybrid quantum-classical workflows remains a significant barrier for application researchers due to the required expertise in quantum algorithms, nuances in quantum programming, and hardware-aware system integration. At the same time, AI and primarily LLM based agents are increasingly capable of interpreting natural-language intent, reasoning over complex workflows, and translating high-level objectives into executable code and building computational pipelines. In this work, we introduce SQD Agent, an LLM-based agentic framework that translates natural-language user intent into executable workflows for Quantum Chemistry applications where algorithms from the Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) family are used. By automating this translation, SQD Agent reduces the level of human expertise and configuration overhead required, thereby simplifying experimentation in hybrid quantum-classical settings for application researchers new to quantum. SQD Agent adopts a modular and extensible architecture that supports seamless integration of heterogeneous quantum backends, classical solvers, and workflow components, ensuring adaptability to rapidly evolving quantum ecosystems. The framework further incorporates interactive capabilities for on-demand profiling, bottleneck analysis, resource optimization, intelligent result caching, and convergence visualization. Key features include quantum chemistry experiments, error mitigation on real quantum hardware, together with analysis of candidate mitigation schemes in terms of their potential error-recovery behavior and computational budget, helping users understand their practical trade-offs and decide which strategies to explore in subsequent experiments.
item.dc:creator: Kislaya Tiwari, Anupama Ray

item.title: QMA(2) with Limited Shared Entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2609.39668v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$, two computationally unbounded provers submit unentangled quantum witnesses to a polynomial-time quantum verifier. We ask whether allowing limited shared entanglement between the two provers changes the power of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$. To this end, we formalize $\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$, a variant in which the provers initially share $h$ EPR pairs, as suggested by Aaronson, Beigi, Drucker, Fefferman, and Shor (ToC~2009). We show that polynomially many shared EPR pairs give the provers no cheating advantage: $\mathsf{QMA}(2)\subseteq\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$ for $h=\operatorname{poly}(n)$. For logarithmically many pairs, the power of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ remains unchanged, strengthening this inclusion to $\mathsf{QMA}(2)=\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$ for $h=O(\log n)$. Finally, we introduce a variant that also allows classical communication between the provers when preparing the witnesses. This setting is particularly revealing for logarithmic-size witnesses: assuming $\mathsf{NP}\nsubseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, we show that superlogarithmically many shared EPR pairs strictly reduce the model's computational power.
item.dc:creator: Alex Della Schiava, Ranitha Mataraarachchi

item.title: Theory of spacetime quantum fault tolerance
item.description: arXiv:2609.39758v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a unified algebraic theory of Clifford spacetime quantum fault tolerance, which underpins universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. We construct a spacetime chain complex from a tensor network representation of a circuit that encodes fault propagation, detector syndromes, and logical actions through the associated gauge and stabilizer structure. We show that this theory (1) unifies various formulations of quantum fault tolerance including spacetime codes, Gottesman's gadget framework, fault complexes, and ZX calculus; (2) connects spacetime distances to the gadget-level correctness properties in Gottesman's formalism; (3) naturally accommodates a range of fault models, in particular phenomenological and circuit-level models, bringing these often separately formulated descriptions into a common algebraic framework through different tensor decompositions and fault assignments; and (4) recovers many known fault tolerance constructions and results as special cases, including repeated syndrome extraction, correlated detectors for transversal and fold-transversal gates, Steane- and Knill-type syndrome extraction gadgets, and single-shot error correction.
item.dc:creator: Yijia Xu, Yixu Wang, Zi-Wen Liu

item.title: The quantum-classical bipartite universe and the logical emergence of $\hbar$ from classical temporality
item.description: arXiv:2610.05083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a foundational reinterpretation of quantum dynamics based on the standard von Neumann formalism, positing a structural logical bipartition between a classical observational environment and a quantum observed system. Against universalist frameworks, we argue that theoretical consistency requires distinct propositional logics: Boolean logic governs the environment, while non-Boolean logic applies to the observed system. Within this framework, an ideal classical clock is represented as an open system whose energy spectrum is uniformly discretized. The dynamics follow from the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation under the constraint that the Hamiltonian remains observable. Although the clock's temporal evolution is driven by dissipative coupling to the measurement apparatus, it admits a deterministic solution corresponding to information-preserving cyclic dynamics. This deterministic regime may emerge as a logical attractor, stabilized by the Boolean structure inherent to the measurement interaction. Ultimately, $\hbar$ is derived as a fundamental scaling parameter from the classical clock's action operator, revealing that the quantum of action reflects the discrete logical structure underlying classical temporality. Furthermore, this framework establishes an exact mapping with 't Hooft's cellular automaton formalism, offering an alternative ontological interpretation that not require hidden variables and superdeterministic assumptions. The resulting distinction between quantum dynamics (as potential recontextualization) and classical dynamics (as temporal actualization) provides a novel logical approach to the measurement problem.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Chilla

item.title: Causal memory and structural complexity of correlated quantum sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.06519v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: What makes one quantum process more complex than another? We adopt an operational approach inspired by classical complexity science, which characterises structure through the memory required for causal generation. We develop a fully-quantum extension of computational mechanics for quantum space series: Correlated sequences of quantum outputs that do not return to interact with their generator. For stationary, memoryful quantum space series admitting finite-dimensional, primitive causal models, we show that any memory-minimal causal generator can be chosen to produce outputs isometrically, without a discarded environment. The resulting canonical matrix product state representation uniquely determines the irreducible memory required for generation. In particular, the minimum memory entropy is exactly the entanglement entropy across the past-future bipartition, giving entanglement a direct operational interpretation as irreducible memory for causal generation. The same structure determines the minimum memory dimension through the corresponding Schmidt rank. Within this class, we further show that the fundamental entropy rate vanishes, that causal generation is symmetric under time reversal, and that all memoryful processes possess infinite quantum Markov order with respect to arbitrary sharp measurements. These results establish an operational framework for quantifying intrinsic quantum structure, revealing deep connections between causal generation, complexity, memory, entropy, and entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Thomas J. Elliott

item.title: The Mermin-Peres Magic Square Game With Three or More Players
item.description: arXiv:2610.06534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a generalization of the Mermin-Peres magic square game to $N$ players, in which the square is replaced by an $N$-dimensional hypercube. We show that the winning probability of the optimal classical strategy remains $8/9$ for all $N$, while for $N \ge 3$, a generalization of the quantum strategy for $N = 2$ achieves a winning probability between $1/3$ and $3/4$. This loss of quantum advantage for $N \ge 3$ is a consequence of monogamy.
item.dc:creator: Itamar Lorian, J. E. Avron

item.title: Energy-constrained two-way capacities of pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.06832v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the two-way quantum, entanglement-distribution, private, and secret-key capacities of the pure-loss bosonic channel under an unconditional mean transmitted-photon-number constraint. For transmissivity $\eta$ and mean photon number $N$, all four capacities coincide and are given by $g(N)-g((1-\eta)N)$, where $g$ is the entropy of a thermal mode. This resolves the longstanding energy-constrained capacity problem by establishing the optimality of the reverse-coherent-information rate introduced in 2009. Our central tool is sector teleportation simulation, which we develop specifically to transfer the input-energy constraint to the shared entanglement resource, thereby preserving the constraint throughout converse arguments for general adaptive protocols. For every $N>0$, we further show that the corresponding strong-converse thresholds coincide with the unconstrained value $-\log_2(1-\eta)$. For parallel protocols with a hard total-photon-number cutoff, the same energy-constrained capacity formula instead satisfies an exponential strong converse. As an extension, we determine the energy-constrained two-way capacities of the quantum-limited amplifier, showing that classical assistance does not improve its unassisted quantum and private rates. Together, these results establish a unified finite-energy framework for adaptive bosonic communication and reveal how energy constraints fundamentally reshape both attainable rates and converse bounds.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Energy-constrained two-way capacity bounds for noisy Gaussian channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.08786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A gap between achievable rates and converse bounds persists for energy-constrained bosonic communication in the presence of excess noise. We derive a unified adaptive weak-converse bound for thermal attenuation, noisy amplification, and additive Gaussian noise under an unconditional mean transmitted-photon-number constraint. The bound applies to arbitrary adaptive protocols with quantum memories and constrains the two-way quantum, entanglement-distribution, private, and secret-key capacities. It vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region and approaches the corresponding PLOB bound at infinite energy. At finite energy, it improves the evaluated Gaussian squashed-entanglement and PLOB bounds in relevant parameter regimes, while comparison with hashing rates quantifies the remaining gap to achievability. The result provides a common energy-dependent benchmark for noisy bosonic Gaussian channels and extends finite-energy converse methods beyond the quantum-limited setting.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.15586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.
item.dc:creator: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Villa Park, California, USA), Byeongyong Park (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

item.title: Autonomous optomechanical Maxwell Demon engine
item.description: arXiv:2610.18237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a fully autonomous model of a mechanical Maxwell demon engine that converts heat absorbed by a qubit into population inversion in an attached quantum battery. A damped mechanical oscillator acts as a pointer that incorporates the essential demon function of information acquisition about the qubit state and subsequent feedback into the system dynamics, replacing external measurements and control operations. This is achieved by means of a Holstein-type Hamiltonian, which makes the pointer's equilibrium position depend on the qubit state and thereby induces a state-dependent resonance shift. The mechanism enables a selective energy transfer to an attached spin system that acts as the quantum battery. We derive both local and global Lindblad master equations for the coupled system and identify the parameter regimes in which the engine operates efficiently. The figure of merit is the resulting steady-state population inversion of the battery, quantified in terms of ergotropy. Based on these results, we discuss the necessary conditions for practical implementations of the demon engine on realistic experimental platforms.
item.dc:creator: Sander Stammbach, Giulio Gasbarri, Stefan Nimmrichter

item.title: PULSUS: Direct Frequency-Domain Multidimensional Spectroscopy Beyond the Impulsive Rotating-Wave Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18712v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce PULSUS, a direct frequency-domain framework for multidimensional spectroscopy of open quantum systems beyond the impulsive rotating-wave approximation. Coherence-frequency intervals are represented through Liouvillian resolvents, while finite Gaussian pulses are incorporated through operator-valued functions of the field-free Liouvillian. This enables direct evaluation on Cartesian grids or arbitrary spectral coordinates while retaining molecular evolution during the pulse envelopes and, when required, the complete light--matter interaction. The implementation is validated against analytical and independent time-domain benchmarks and supports targeted spectral sampling that reduces the number of evaluated coordinates when the response is spectrally localized. A controlled hierarchy of finite-pulse, rotating-wave, short-pulse, and impulsive models separates the errors introduced by each approximation. For a coupled electronic dimer, the total impulsive-RWA error is nonmonotonic in pulse duration: an intermediate regime provides the highest accuracy, whereas ultrashort pulses expose coupling-enabled beyond-RWA pathways and longer pulses develop substantial finite-pulse corrections. These results show that the impulsive and rotating-wave approximations cannot be assumed to improve simultaneously and should be tested when quantitatively interpreting multidimensional spectra. PULSUS provides a direct frequency-domain framework for carrying out that comparison.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Castillo-Gonzalez, Eric R. Bittner

item.title: Searching for Ultra-Light Axions with Twisted Cavity Resonators of Anyon Rotational Symmetry with Bulk Modes of Non-Zero Helicity
item.description: arXiv:2208.01640v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: M\"obius-ring resonators stem from a well-studied geometrical structure with a one-sided topology, the M\"obius strip, and have been shown to exhibit fermion rotational symmetry with respect to an untwisted ring resonator, which exhibits boson rotational symmetry [1]. Here, we present twisted hollow resonators with equilateral triangular cross-sections, leading to cavities with anyon rotational symmetry. Unlike conventional cavity resonators, these structures permit bulk resonant modes with a non-zero complex electromagnetic overlap $\mathcal C_p=\int_V\mathbf{E}_p\cdot\mathbf{B}_p^*\,d\tau$. The real and imaginary parts of this overlap couple to different observable quadratures. Although the negative-frequency component of a real axion field is immaterial for haloscopes employing a static DC magnetic field, it must be retained for a pumped resonator because the complex forms of Maxwell's equations differ for positive and negative frequencies and produce distinct upper and lower mixing branches. Retaining both branches shows that the real overlap produces amplitude-modulated sidebands, whereas the imaginary helicity of the modes studied here produces phase-modulated sidebands through the axion-photon chiral anomaly. A sensitive ultra-light dark-matter experiment may therefore be realised with an ultra-stable oscillator and a phase-sensitive readout. The sensitivity curves calculated here require the assumed noise floor to be interpreted as phase-modulation noise rather than amplitude-modulation noise, and consequently require sufficiently low residual oscillator phase noise at the axion Fourier frequency. The scheme removes the usual requirement for an external magnetic field and permits superconducting resonators with reduced surface loss and enhanced axion sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: J. F. Bourhill, E. C. I. Paterson, M. Goryachev, M. E. Tobar

item.title: Statistical Description of Fermi System over a Surface in a Uniform External Field
item.description: arXiv:2506.12608v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A statistical approach to the description of the thermodynamic properties of the Fermi particle system occupying a half-space over a plane of finite size in a uniform external field is proposed. The number of particles per unit area is assumed to be arbitrary, in particular, small. General formulas are obtained for entropy, energy, thermodynamic potential, heat capacities under various conditions and the distribution of the particle number density over the surface. In the continuum limit of a large surface area, the temperature dependences of heat capacities and density distribution are calculated. The cases of gravitational and electric fields are considered.
item.dc:creator: Yu. M. Poluektov, A. A. Soroka

item.title: Green's functions for magnetic Dirac operators and bulk-edge correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2509.17151v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the resolvent kernel (Green's function) of magnetic Dirac operators on a half-plane with boundary conditions interpolating between infinite mass and zigzag cases, excluding the latter. We show that these kernels have all the required properties so that the proof of bulk-edge correspondence from the infinite mass case shown recently can be repeated ad litteram. The zigzag case exhibits qualitatively different behavior and will be addressed in future work.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marie Barbaroux, Horia D. Cornean, Lo\"ic Le Treust, Nicolas Raymond, Edgardo Stockmeyer

item.title: A Versatile Variational Quantum Kernel Framework for Non-Trivial Classification
item.description: arXiv:2511.10831v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum kernel methods are a promising branch of quantum machine learning, but their per- formance across data types and encoding choices remains incompletely understood. To address this gap, we developed an algorithmic framework for variational quantum kernels utilizing resource- efficient ans\"atze for complex classification tasks and introduced a parameter scaling technique to accelerate convergence. We conducted a comprehensive benchmark of this framework on eight chal- lenging, real-world and high-dimensional datasets covering tabular, image, time series, and graph data. Our results show that the proposed quantum kernel demonstrated competitive classification accuracy compared to standard classical kernels in classical simulation, such as the radial basis function (RBF) kernel. This work demonstrates that properly designed quantum kernels can func- tion as versatile, high-performance tools, laying a foundation for quantum-enhanced applications in machine learning. Further research is needed to fully assess the practical performance of quantum methods.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Yuhan, Matthew Otten

item.title: Strong-field regime within effective field theory
item.description: arXiv:2512.07958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Building upon the Covariant Derivative Expansion, we develop a method to compute effective actions that is able to capture non-perturbative effects induced by strong background fields. We demonstrate the method in scalar QED, by deriving the full second-derivative corrections to the scalar Heisenberg--Euler effective action. The corresponding result is interpreted as an effective field theory with three characteristic scales, two of which are large (mass and field strength) in comparison with the remaining one (derivatives of the field). As an application, we show that, at this order, the transseries structure of the Schwinger pair production rate is preserved, even if the involved coefficients are modified. Our analysis also helps clarify recent disagreements concerning the coefficients of this effective action.
item.dc:creator: Sebasti\'an Franchino-Vi\~nas, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

item.title: Quantum speed limit time for bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations in matter with nonstandard interactions
item.description: arXiv:2602.03748v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the three-flavor neutrino oscillation framework, we investigate the transition probabilities of an initial muon neutrino flavor state in the presence of nonstandard interactions (NSIs) characterized by complex off-diagonal ($|\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}|e^{i\phi_{\alpha\beta}}$) and diagonal parameters ($|\epsilon_{\alpha\alpha}-\epsilon_{\beta\beta}|$), including a $CP$-violating phase and a constant matter potential, under both normal (NO) and inverted mass ordering (IO) scenarios. Within these scenarios and through the lens of mode entanglement, bipartite entanglement measures such as entanglement entropy and capacity of entanglement are quantified in terms of the transition probabilities, which can be measured in neutrino oscillation experiments. Using these two bipartite entanglement measures, we further explore the quantum speed limit (QSL) time, which describes how rapidly bipartite entanglement evolves during neutrino oscillations. We illustrate our results using the baseline lengths and energies corresponding to ongoing long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments, such as T2K, NO$\nu$A, and the upcoming DUNE experiment. In the presence of a $CP$-violating phase and a constant matter potential, both with and without NSI effects, we compare the QSL time behavior for bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations for NO and IO. The most pronounced discrepancies in the QSL time for bipartite entanglement arise from the off-diagonal NSI parameter $\epsilon_{\mu\tau}$ across both the NO and IO scenarios. We emphasize that among all the experiments considered, NO$\nu$A and DUNE exhibit a rapid suppression of bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations in the standard oscillation scenario with NO at the end of their baseline lengths for the corresponding best-fit value of $CP$-violating phase. Our results hint at a possible imprint of new physics in neutrino oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Kumar Jha, Lekhashri Konwar, Rukmani Mohanta

item.title: Structured-Light Magnetometry in a Coherently Controlled Atomic Medium
item.description: arXiv:2603.25781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A structured-light-based approach to magneto-optical rotation (MOR) magnetometry is proposed, in which magnetically induced polarization rotation is converted into a directly observable spatial displacement. A radially polarized Laguerre--Gaussian beam propagating through cold $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ atoms in the presence of a longitudinal magnetic field experiences circular birefringence, which induces a relative phase shift between the $\sigma_+$ and $\sigma_-$ polarization components. This phase shift manifests itself as the angular rotation of a petal-shaped interference pattern, enabling the MOR angle to be determined directly from the spatial intensity distribution. Unlike conventional MOR detection techniques based on balanced polarimetry or Stokes-parameter reconstruction, the proposed method requires only a fixed-axis polarization projection and avoids computationally intensive polarization analysis. By translating polarization rotation into a topology-dependent spatial observable, the scheme enables direct and spatially resolved magnetic-field measurements. Furthermore, the use of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) allows low-loss operation while preserving high sensitivity. These characteristics make the proposed technique a promising platform for optical magnetometry and structured-light-based quantum sensing.
item.dc:creator: Parkhi Bhardwaj, Shubhrangshu Dasgupta

item.title: Quantum simulation of traversable-wormhole-inspired quantum teleportation in a chaotic binary sparse SYK model
item.description: arXiv:2604.10090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the experimental signature of holographically motivated quantum teleportation on a quantum processor, driven by the highly entangled, chaotic dynamics of a many-body system. Specifically, we implement the traversable-wormhole (TW) protocol utilizing a \textit{chaotic} binary sparse $N = 8$ Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model. This optimized approach dramatically reduces circuit depth for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware while rigorously preserving the spectral chaos required for gravitational duality. Diagnosing the teleportation signal via mutual information, we find that while inherent noise in NISQ hardware precludes perfect quantitative agreement with exact numerical simulations, our experimental results provide evidence for the essential qualitative signature: a sign-dependent asymmetry. This work establishes a practical framework for holographic quantum simulations, offering a novel empirical testbed for exploring holographic quantum gravity.
item.dc:creator: Moongul Byun, Hyeonsoo Lee, Keun-Young Kim

item.title: Probing critical phases in quasiperiodic systems via subsystem information capacity
item.description: arXiv:2605.06075v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We systematically investigate the entanglement and information dynamics of quasiperiodic systems across their extended, critical, and localized phases, aiming to identify dynamical signatures that can reveal the multifractal spatial structure of critical states and distinguish critical phases from the extended and localized regimes. Focusing on the generalized Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model, we complement the half-chain entanglement entropy with the spatially resolved subsystem information capacity (SIC) and demonstrate that critical states exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity absent in the extended and localized phases. In the steady state, the SIC reveals a stepwise ramp as a function of subsystem size, reflecting an underlying fragmentation of the chain into weakly connected subregions. Dynamically, information initially localized within such a subregion can undergo coherent long-lived oscillations, dubbed subregion echoes, whose period scales with the subregion length, in quantitative agreement with a quasiparticle picture of confined quasiparticle reflections. We trace this internal fragmentation to the incommensurately distributed zeros (IDZs) in the off-diagonal hopping terms of the Hamiltonian. To establish the generality of the SIC as a diagnostic tool, we further apply it to a mobility-edge phase with coexisting extended and localized states and to a critical phase that does not originate from IDZ fragmentation, and show that the SIC can cleanly distinguish these scenarios through their distinct steady-state profiles, initial-site sensitivities, and the presence or absence of subregion echoes. Our results demonstrate that the SIC serves as a powerful real-space probe for diagnosing critical phases and uncovering the bottlenecked connectivity that underlies the multifractal structure of critical states.
item.dc:creator: Huaijin Dong, Long Zhang

item.title: Soft-Radiation-Induced Decoherence of Heavy-Quark Spin Entanglement at the Electron-Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2606.29944v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the soft-gluon theorem, we identify a soft-recoil mechanism by which unresolved gluon radiation induces decoherence in the spin correlations of heavy quark-antiquark pairs produced by longitudinally polarized virtual photons in deep-inelastic scattering. Upon tracing over the unresolved gluon, the reduced spin density matrix is block diagonal in the mirror parity of the production plane and is governed by two coefficients: a parity-odd normal-spin flip, which reduces the normal-axis correlation, and a parity-even stochastic rotation of the spin-correlation plane about its normal, which suppresses the in-plane spin coherences while leaving the normal-axis correlation unchanged. From the complete tree-level next-to-soft amplitude with the exact color-octet structure we derive both coefficients, together with the trace and antisymmetric in-plane terms, in closed form. The parity-odd coefficient is the larger one, by a factor of at least $3.5$, and grows as the inverse square of the heavy-quark transverse momentum. We estimate the resulting reduction of concurrence and Bell-CHSH violation, and propose an infrared-safe, radiation-binned EIC observable, formed at fixed Born kinematics after longitudinal-transverse separation, which isolates the two channels. We estimate its size, including multiple wide-angle emissions in an independent-emission model, the conditions under which detector and kinematic effects cancel, and the statistics required. The latter, however, exceed the yield of exclusive heavy-baryon pairs at nominal EIC luminosity by several orders of magnitude, makes the observable elusive for the measurement accessible in that channel.
item.dc:creator: Sanskriti Agrawal, Muneeb Zahoor, Raktim Abir

item.title: Topological zero-reflection points in multi-terminal quantum wire junctions
item.description: arXiv:2606.31586v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study scattering in noninteracting multi-terminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for $N \ge 4$ terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the $(E,t')$ parameter space, where $E$ is the incident particle energy and $t'$ is the junction hopping amplitude. These points exhibit an even-odd dependence on $N$ and converge asymptotically to a common limiting value in the large-$N$ limit. We show that the reflectionless points are characterized by an integer winding number associated with the phase of the reflection amplitude, providing a topological description for their stability against weak on-site disorder. We also consider junctions with broken time-reversal symmetry and find that a magnetic flux can induce additional reflectionless points, including for the $N = 3$ case. For a four-terminal junction threaded by a $\pi$-flux, we identify a unique parameter regime in which the reflection amplitude vanishes over the entire energy band. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures through the behavior of Friedel oscillations and examine the stability of these reflectionless points in the presence of weak interactions.
item.dc:creator: Abhiram Soori, Udit Khanna, Diptiman Sen

item.title: Hermitian Hulls of Cyclic Codes and Exact Dual Distances of Extended Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2607.12242v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $[n,k,d]$ linear code over $\F_{q^2}$ with parity-check matrix $H$. The rank $r=\Rank(HH^{\dagger})$ measures how far the Hermitian dual $\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ is from being Hermitian self-orthogonal, and it is the least number of coordinates that must be adjoined to $\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ to make it Hermitian self-orthogonal; equivalently, the Hermitian hull $\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ has dimension $(n-k)-r$. In this paper, we develop a structure theory of the Hermitian hull of a cyclic code and apply it to the construction of quantum stabilizer codes. For a cyclic code with defining set $T\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$, we show that $r$ is additive over the orbits of the involution $\tau(\nu)=-q\nu$ on the $q^2$-cyclotomic cosets and satisfies a parity constraint. A parameter dictionary exhibits $r$ as a gauge trading one-for-one against the code length, and a complementation duality shows that the complement of $T$ realises the logical-qubit count of the quantum code. The extreme values of $r$ are settled by closed subset-sum criteria, and the $\tau$-invariant defining sets are shown to be the unique locus on which the Hermitian dual is again cyclic. On the distance side, we determine the Hermitian dual distance of an $r$-fold extension of an arbitrary linear code exactly, and we prove that the admissible extension vectors lie in the image of $HH^{\dagger}$, which reduces the search space from $q^{2(n-k)}$ to $q^{2r}$. Applied to cyclic, quasi-cyclic and BCH codes, the construction improves $23$ best-known parameters in Grassl's code tables, one of them provably optimal.
item.dc:creator: Liangdong Lu, Ruipan Yang, Yang Liu, Qiang Fu, Guanmin Guo

item.title: Tripartite Form Universality in Holographic Entropy Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2609.22504v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To elucidate the meaning of holographic entropy inequalities (beyond subadditivity) which characterize the entanglement structure of geometric states in holography, arXiv:2309.06296 proposed the "tripartite form" for these inequalities, consisting of tripartite information and conditional tripartite information terms with unit coefficients. While this provides a compact and useful packaging of the inequalities, it is not a priori guaranteed that all inequalities can be recast in this form. Here we conjecture that they can, and present substantial evidence, by proving that the two known infinite families of holographic entropy inequalities found in arXiv:2309.15145 can indeed be written in the tripartite form. This is significant because such recasting is particularly nontrivial for these families. Apart from providing the explicit tripartite form expressions for every member of these two infinite families, we detail how we arrived at them, in the process deriving several useful identities which may serve as stepping stones to formulate further repackaging of the corresponding information quantities. We also illustrate the power of the tripartite form by proving a number of structural properties satisfied by any holographic entropy inequality.
item.dc:creator: Veronika E. Hubeny, Yu Liu

item.title: Placement-driven reversal of preferred spin alignment in monolayer hBN vacancy pairs
item.description: arXiv:2609.33714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The negatively charged boron vacancy is an optically addressable spin centre in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), but bringing two vacancies together introduces electronic interactions absent from the isolated-defect picture. Here we use density-functional theory at total charge q = -2 to show that atomic-scale placement reverses the preferred collinear spin alignment in monolayer hBN. Among seven configurations, the closest pair, separated by 4.3 angstrom, favours parallel alignment by 27.6 meV within the semilocal approximation. Moving one vacancy by a single lattice vector reverses the preference, and a 7.5 angstrom pair favours antiparallel alignment by 50.7 meV. Numerical controls change these two reference splittings by less than 1 meV; hybrid-functional calculations retain their signs while substantially changing their magnitudes. Local distortions connect the antiparallel preference at 7.5 angstrom to changes in vacancy-state hybridization along an intervening atomic chain. The closest pair instead exhibits a contact-localized spin-density contrast and constrained angular energies that depart from the bilinear Heisenberg form. These results identify a placement-sensitive regime of interacting defects and provide a microscopic foundation for investigating coupled spin centres in atomically thin materials.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Hashemi

item.title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response
item.description: arXiv:2610.01862v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. We derive the cumulative occupation up to a cut that moves to greater Krylov depth with time, tracking the probability accumulated behind the propagating front. This quantity separates the release dynamics of the finite sector from subsequent propagation through the tail. The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale, while the finite sector shapes the resulting distribution. The early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, while the late edge reflects slow resonances and interference and can also exhibit logarithmic enhancements. Thus, one- and two-site sectors can share the same leading resonance in their continued-fraction descriptions yet produce distinct cumulative occupation patterns. We illustrate this framework in thermal AdS$_2$, where a dressed oscillator yields, in the weak-coupling limit, a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Alishahiha

item.title: Competitive scaling of small-subsystem-optimization heuristics for LABS
item.description: arXiv:2610.14361v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) problem, often formulated as a spin-lattice energy-minimization problem, is a combinatorial optimization problem with a very rugged energy landscape. We demonstrate that iterative optimization of very small subsystems of n spins that are decoupled from the rest of the system achieves global optimization of LABS with a time-to-solution scaling that is competitive with heuristics that optimize the global system of N spins directly. Our isolated-subsystem heuristic with n = 4 achieves a time scaling of O(1.333^N ) on the interval N = [27, 60], while the current state-of-the-art classical and quantum scalings are respectively O(1.34^N ) and O(1.21^N ). Our results suggest that specialized optimization hardware with only small numbers of logical spins may be of practical relevance.

item.title: An Aubry-Andr\'e localized optical lattice clock
item.description: arXiv:2610.17499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical lattice clocks in space could improve satellite navigation systems and enable new tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational-wave detection and tests of relativity. In microgravity, atoms can tunnel to degenerate neighboring lattice sites, broadening the clock transition and limiting coherence times. We demonstrate Aubry-Andr\'e localization in a bichromatic optical lattice formed by two magic-wavelength lasers, suppressing tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock emulating free fall. We recover a Fourier-limited clock Rabi spectrum and measure Ramsey coherence times of up to 2 s in shallow lattices, with up to 100-fold improvement over the delocalized regime. These results establish Aubry-Andr\'e localization as a practical route to controlling tunneling in future space-based clocks, and open a path to operating terrestrial clocks at shallower lattice depths.
